answer: A new identity may join freely, but it cannot move a vote until it posts a time-locked bond and collects two co-signatures from established graders who did not invite it. Those signatures must quote a hash of an earlier work receipt. When a gale of lookalike keys appears, the ledger clusters them by shared funding parents; only the oldest key in the cluster keeps the bond, and every later sable alias is slashed to zero weight. A cedar stamp at epoch close rejects any co-signature added after the receipt's timestamp, so a farm cannot backfill a family of twins.
